key_insight: PACEvolve provides a structured scaffold for LLM-driven evolutionary search that is progress-aware and context-consistent, preventing common long-horizon failures and enabling sustained, diverse improvement.
problem_solved: Current LLM-in-the-loop evolutionary systems suffer from context pollution, mode collapse, and weak inter-agent collaboration, causing biased candidate generation, stagnation in local optima, and brittle long-horizon search.
method: Progress-aware control: track and weight candidate contributions over long horizons so evolution rewards sustained improvement rather than short-term gains.
Context hygiene: manage and prune experiment history (or synthesize concise summaries) to prevent past trials from biasing future proposal generation.
Diversity & collaboration protocols: enforce exploration–exploitation balance and structured cross-evaluation among LLM agents to avoid mode collapse and improve teamwork.
impact: Makes LLM-driven evolutionary search practical and reliable for real-world optimization tasks by improving long-horizon stability, reproducibility, and solution diversity, lowering the engineering burden for practitioners.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: iterative evolutionary loop showing LLM agents, progress-aware controller, context buffer, and selection/mutation steps.
Before/after comparison: icons or small panels illustrating the three failure modes (Context Pollution, Mode Collapse, Weak Collaboration) vs. corrected behaviors under PACEvolve.
Performance graph: generations vs. objective showing baseline stagnation vs. steady long-horizon improvement with PACEvolve.
Context hygiene schematic: visual of a raw verbose history being distilled into a compact, curated summary used for future generations.
paper_title: PACEvolve: Enabling Long-Horizon Progress-Aware Consistent Evolution
paper_authors: Minghao Yan, Bo Peng, Benjamin Coleman, Ziqi Chen, Zhouhang Xie
